rv.q: There’s no denying the dazzling structural precision of Holcroft’s writing, as well as the lightness of touch she brings.
It’s ingenious and often very funny, as the cast play with levels of reality.

For the best part of two hours, its agenda is camouflaged by relentless metatheatre that runs in circles. It is only at the end that we arrive at the pay-off. It is a drama of many layers: when it is at its most complicated, we are watching a play within a play within play, all constructed around a wedding.
'A Mirror' is a timely production packed with intrigue and passion.
Director Jeremy Herrin has got his cast to play-act this set-up with total conviction, but it is nevertheless a hollow one.
A compelling story, but unnecessarily convoluted at times.
...it descends into a bewildering chaotic assault on theatrical censorship.

cn.t: Holcroft's clever play-within-a-play about censorship and authoritarian control earns mostly positive reviews for its inventive structure, though some find the meta-theatrical layers confusing and the execution uneven.
